content: Labetalol is prescribed to treat high blood pressure. It belongs to a class of medications known as beta blockers. This medication works by relaxing blood vessels and slowing the heart rate, which improves blood flow and reduces blood pressure. Labetalol is available in tablet form and is taken orally. It is typically taken two or three times a day. You should carefully follow the instructions on your prescription label and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take labetalol exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. While labetalol helps control high blood pressure, it does not cure the condition. Continue taking labetalol even if you feel well, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Labetalol is sometimes used to treat angina (chest pain) and patients with tetanus. Discuss the potential risks of using this medication for your condition with your doctor. It may also be prescribed for other uses; ask your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking labetalol, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to labetalol or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially other medications for high blood pressure or heart disease, cimetidine (Tagamet), nitroglycerin, medications for asthma, headaches, allergies, colds, or pain, as well as any vitamins or supplements. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had heart, kidney, or liver disease; asthma or other lung diseases; severe allergies; diabetes; or pheochromocytoma. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, let your doctor know. If you become pregnant while taking labetalol, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking labetalol. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Do not drive or operate machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can increase the drowsiness caused by this medication. Unless instructed otherwise by your doctor, continue your normal diet while taking labetalol. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Labetalol may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms and they are severe or persistent: dizziness, tingling of the scalp or skin, lightheadedness, excessive tiredness, headache, upset stomach, or a stuffy nose. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience shortness of breath or wheezing, swelling of the feet or lower legs, sudden weight gain, or chest pain. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store labetalol in the container it came in, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist about the correct disposal method. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your blood pressure should be checked regularly to monitor your response to labetalol. Your doctor may ask you to check your pulse (heart rate). Ask your doctor or pharmacist to teach you how to do this. If your pulse is faster or slower than it should be, contact your doctor. Do not share your medication with anyone else. Ask your pharmacist any questions you have about refilling your prescription. It is important to maintain a written list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, including vitamins, minerals, and dietary supplements. Bring this list with you to every doctor’s appointment or if you are admitted to a hospital. This information is also crucial to have in case of emergencies.
